arms.predicted: Across arrival rates 5-130 req/s, AD will produce lower mean ITL than AL at every rate, with the absolute ITL gap (ITL_AL - ITL_AD) increasing monotonically with rate. Simultaneously, AD will produce higher mean TTFT than AL at every rate. The ITL-vs-rate curve for each mode will fit ITL = a/(1-b*lambda) + c with R-squared > 0.95, where b_AL > b_AD.
arms.observed: ITL ordering AL > AD: confirmed at all 8 rates across all 3 seeds (0 violations). Mean ITL (ms): AL=[12.49, 12.80, 13.44, 14.79, 16.18, 17.44, 18.43, 19.45] vs AD=[12.43, 12.67, 13.15, 14.16, 15.17, 16.10, 16.88, 17.77] for rates [5,10,20,40,60,80,100,130]. ITL gap: [0.058, 0.129, 0.283, 0.634, 1.014, 1.334, 1.554, 1.682] ms, monotonically increasing. TTFT ordering AD > AL: confirmed at all 8 rates across all 3 seeds (0 violations). TTFT gap (AD-AL): [9.61, 9.36, 9.27, 8.70, 7.46, 5.88, 5.36, 4.21] ms, narrowing with rate. Formula fit: AD achieves R^2=0.956 (> 0.95 threshold); AL achieves R^2=0.927 (slightly below threshold). b_AL/b_AD = 1.21, confirming AL has higher effective work per request. All 300 requests completed with 0 drops across all 48 runs.
arms.diagnostic_note: AL formula fit achieves R^2=0.927, slightly below the 0.95 threshold. This minor shortfall is consistent with mixed-server prefill+decode interactions under AL. The core directional predictions (ITL ordering, TTFT ordering, gap monotonicity) are fully confirmed.

arms.predicted: At rate=5 req/s (near-zero load), the mean ITL gap between AL and AD will be less than 0.5 ms, significantly smaller than the gap at rate=130 (~1.7 ms). This confirms that the disaggregation advantage is driven by load-dependent batch interference.
arms.observed: Mean ITL gap at rate=5: 0.058 ms (seeds 42/43/44: 0.057, 0.058, 0.058 ms), all well below the 0.5 ms threshold. Mean ITL gap at rate=130: 1.682 ms. Rate=5 gap is 3.4% of rate=130 gap, confirming the effect is almost entirely load-driven. All 6 rate=5 runs completed 300/300 requests with 0 drops.

discrepancy_analysis: Both arms confirmed. The only minor discrepancy from the predictions is AL formula fit R^2=0.927 vs the 0.95 target — a secondary quantitative threshold that does not affect the primary directional claims. The paper's queueing model is a better fit for AD (dedicated decode server, cleaner M/G/1-like regime) than for AL (mixed prefill+decode batches introduce moderate non-linearity). The b-ratio AL/AD=1.21 validates the paper's core mechanism that AL carries higher effective work per request.
